subtitle: Lesson 99 · Transactions, Locking, and Isolation Levels

eyebrow: Step 1 -- enable it at the database level
code:
ALTER DATABASE AdventureWorks2012
SET ALLOW_SNAPSHOT_ISOLATION ON;
caption: A one-time, database-wide prerequisite -- not a session setting.
Row versioning, not locking -- a fixed point-in-time copy.

code:
-- SNAPSHOT reads from a VERSIONED copy, not the live row --
-- so there's no shared lock for a writer to wait on,
-- and no exclusive lock for the reader to wait on either.
caption: Readers don't block writers. Writers don't block readers.

eyebrow: The one conflict it can't avoid
code:
-- Two SNAPSHOT transactions, same starting snapshot,
-- BOTH try to UPDATE ProductID 680.
-- The second one to commit its write gets:
Msg 3960: Snapshot isolation transaction aborted
  due to update conflict.
caption: A write-write conflict -- SQL Server won't overwrite silently.

subtitle: A database setting that changes what READ COMMITTED itself means.
